Date December 9, 1937.
Subject Summary of the National Salvation and Anti-Japanese Movements
in Shanghai - January to November, 1937.
Made by D.S.I. Laurier Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I.

The arrest of the seven national salvation movement
leaders by the Chinese authorities towards the end of 1936
had a salutary effect upon national salvation elements in
Shanghai, and the movement generally, apart from the
surreptitious distribution of propaganda, became less
active at the beginning of the current year. The enthu-
siasm of these elements, however, was re-kindled in February
and on the 14th of that month a mass meeting was convened
in Nantao, the ostensible objects of which were an expression
of confidence in the Plenary Session of the 5th Central
Executive Committee of the Kuomintang, held at Nanking on
February 15, and a demonstration of anti-Japanese sentiment.
Slogans and songs of an anti-Japanese and national salvation
nature were sung by some 400 persons who attended the meeting
and the following resolutions were passed during the course of
the proceedings:-
1. That a circular telegram be despatched to various
provincial bodies urging the nation to unite and
oppose Japan.
2. That the National Government be urged to unite with
Great Britain, the United States of America, France and
the Union of Soviet Socialist Republic as well as other
peace-loving countries in order to oppose aggression
and that the 3rd Plenary Session be petitioned to grant
the people freedom of speech and assembly, and to release
all leaders of patriotic movements and other political
offenders, serving terms of imprisonment.
3. That the pro-Japanese clique and all other traitors be
eliminated in order to bring about effective national
salvation.

日期：1937年12月9日。
主题：1937年1月至11月上海救国及反日运动综述。
由特别分部督察长 Laurier 编制，经督察长 C. Crawford 转呈。

中国当局在1936年底逮捕七位救国运动领导人，这对上海的救国分子以及整个运动产生了有益的影响；除秘密散发宣传品外，该运动在本年初变得较为沉寂。然而，这些分子的热情在二月重新被点燃，当月14日在南市召开了一次群众大会，其表面目的是表达对2月15日在南京举行的国民党第五届中央执行委员会全体会议的信心，并展示反日情绪。约400名与会者高唱具有反日和救国性质的口号与歌曲，会议期间通过了以下决议：-
1. 向各省团体发出通电解，呼吁全国团结抗日。
2. 敦促国民政府与英国、美利坚合众国、法国及苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟以及其他爱好和平的国家联合起来以反对侵略，并 petition 第三届中央执行委员会全体会议给予人民言论和集会自由，释放所有正在服刑的爱国运动领导人及其他政治犯。
3. 清除亲日派系及所有其他汉奸，以实现有效的救国。

In view of the strong political nature of the activities
of the various national salvation bodies, some 52 of which
were operating in the Settlement in November and their refusal
to heed the Council's warnings the Municipal Police, between
November 5 and 30, raided fourteen offices and seized large
quantities of literature appertaining to their activities.
Raids conducted at each of the remaining thirty-eight offices
revealed that in thirteen cases the offices had been moved to
the interior or to some unknown addresses whilst twenty-five
branches anticipating a visit by the police had dissolved
voluntarily. Two organizations, the Shanghai Women's
Movement Acceleration Association, Room 410, Pootung Guild,
1454 Avenue Edward VII, and the Shanghai Boyscouts Committee
War Time Service Group, 178 Tientsin Road, both of a non-
political nature, have applied for registration in accordance
with Council instructions and their applications are now
under consideration. A list of the national salvation
bodies raided by the Municipal Police is attached to this
report as an appendix.

Since the suppression of the national salvation movement
and the dispersal of its members sporadic attempts have been
made by individuals to revive the movement. These isolated
instances, however, have been successfully suppressed where-
ever encountered with the result that all known anti-Japanese
organizations have now been completely eliminated.

Date 11 NOV. 1937.

P.A.

National Salvation Society

All were to be persuaded to clear
forthwith in 10 minutes & form a good
order.
Propaganda matter found will of course
be seized & documents referring to
propaganda movements.
Other materials will be left after
occupation has been carried out &
search is finished. Documents seized
in course may be returned if relating to
other matters than political movements,
in due course. Occupation will be enforced
that Police will re-enter premises vacated
within 48 hours. Guards will not
be posted but a revisit will be made
after 48 hours. If situation then warrants
satisfactory guards will be asked for
from Stations.

日期 1937年11月11日。
B. I. D.

P.A.

救国会

所有人员均须被劝令在10分钟内立即撤离并维持良好秩序。
发现的宣传品及涉及宣传运动的文件当然予以没收。
其他材料将在占领行动结束且搜查完成后留置。如果在过程中没收的文件与政治运动无关，可在适当时候归还。将强制执行占领，警方将在48小时内重新进入已腾空的场所。不派驻守卫，但将在48小时后进行复查。如果届时情况需要，将向各分局请求派遣适当的守卫。

档案
S.I.

REPORT
Date Nov. 18, 1937.
Subject National Salvation Organizations in the Settlement.
Made by D.S. Hocking Forwarded by C Crawford 18/11

Good

Further to Special Branch Report dated November
4, 1937, on the above subject, all the national salvation
organizations in the Settlement have been visited by
members of the Special Branch. Twelve of these
societies were raided and all propaganda matter found
therein was seized and the offices closed. Twelve have
removed to the interior or to unknown addresses, prior
to the warning by the Municipal Police ordering them to
close down, while the remaining twenty-four have been
dissolved.

Further

Two organizations, the Shanghai Women's Movement
Acceleration Association, Room 410, Pootung Guild, 1454
Avenue Edward VII, and the Shanghai Boyscout Committee
War Time Service Group, 178 Tientsin Road, are applying
for registration, their applications at present being
under consideration.

Attached is a list of national salvation
organizations visited by the Municipal Police.

C 19/11

D.S. Hocking
D. S.

制作人 D.S. Hocking 转呈人 C Crawford 11月18日

好

继1937年11月4日关于上述主题的特别支部报告之后，特别支部成员已走访了租界内所有的救亡组织。其中十二个社团遭到突击搜查，发现的所有宣传品均被没收，办事处被关闭。十二个组织在工部局警务处下令关闭之前已迁往内地或地址不明之处，其余二十四个组织已解散。

Information has been received to the effect that
despite the drastic action taken by the Municipal Police
in suppressing all political activity in the Settlement,
local Chinese national salvation elements are determined to
carry on their propaganda activities in order to keep alive
the morale of the Chinese people living in the foreign
settlements of Shanghai.

In view of the unfavourable development in the local
military situation, these persons have decided to close
down their publicly-known offices and establish secret
communication addresses and rendezvous. As far as can be
ascertained, private houses of individuals, who are members
of various organizations, will be used as much as possible,
and in order to avoid detection by authorities, no centralized
point will be maintained, or kept for a period longer than
necessary. Cells will be established in each alleyway
under the title of tenants' associations and each cell will
be responsible for propaganda activities among residents of
that particular alleyway. Handwritten, instead of printed,
pamphlets in the form of wall newspapers, inscribed with
cartoons, will be used.

It is also learned that hotels and lodging houses will
be utilized and are most favoured for secret meetings or
distribution centres in view of the fact that the rooms in
these places are easy to obtain and easy to remove from.

Political Activities in the Settlement.

Towards the end of October, National Salvation Societies

Anti - Japanese
Bodies Closed

SMP Busy Closing Up
Chinese Societies;
Papers Watched

Official public bodies engaged
in anti-Japanese activities inside
the International Settlement are
being closed down by the Shang-
hai municipal police. Among
several which were told to sus-
pend their activities yesterday
afternoon was the "Shanghai
Committee of All Classes in
Support of Resistance Against the
Enemy (Japan)."

Located in Room 504 at the
Foochow Native Guild, Avenue
Edward VII, the committee, or-
ganised jointly by various Chi-
nese public bodies, had been
during the last three months
engaged in various activities to
aid the Chinese soldiers on the
front. Under its auspices sand-
bags, barbed wire, "comfort-bags"
for the soldiers, cotton padded
jackets and other things had been
collected and forwarded to
the front.

Police visited the premises yes-
terday afternoon and told the
handful of officers of the com-
mittee to wind up their business
and remove the signboard. The
orders were promptly complied
with, and no one turned up at
the office this morning, it is
learned.

Some anxiety is being felt
about the Chinese newspapers
and as to their future position.
Members of the leading Chinese
papers are known to have been
arrested for the last few days
owing to the situation arising from
the withdrawal of the Chinese
troops from the city. None of
the newspapers has been closed
down, however, up to date.

反日
团体被关闭

工部局警务处忙于关闭
华人社团；
报纸受到监视

在国际租界内从事反日活动的官方公共团体正被上海公共租界警务处关闭。昨天下午被告知暂停活动的几个团体中包括“上海各界抗敌后援会”。

该委员会位于爱多亚路浦东同乡会504室，由各个中国公共团体联合组织，在过去三个月中一直从事各种活动以援助前线的中国士兵。在其主持下，沙袋、铁丝网、给士兵的“慰问袋”、棉夹克和其他物品已被收集并运往前线。

警方昨天下午访问了该处所，并告知委员会的几名官员结束业务并拆除招牌。据悉，命令得到迅速遵守，今天上午无人出现在办公室。

人们对中国报纸及其未来地位感到一些焦虑。由于中国军队撤出城市所造成的局势，已知主要中文报纸的成员在过去几天中被捕。然而，截至目前，没有任何报纸被关闭。

（印章：1937年11月13日 总情报局）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

R E P O R T
- - - - - -
September 28, 1937. Section 1. Special Branch.

CHINESE PUBLIC ORGANIZATIONS - POLITICAL
ACTIVITIES.

Following the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities
in Shanghai, the majority of Chinese public organizations,
including the Chamber of Commerce and other bodies of long
and more or less respectable standing, commenced to engage
in political movements and propaganda. Their ranks were
further augmented by numerous other organizations of unsavoury
character which sprang up like mushrooms. Unusual political
activity by these bodies was conspicuous throughout the
International Settlement where practically all the headquarters
or offices of these bodies are located. The existence of
these, in some cases most undesirable organisations, in the
Settlement is due to the recognised fact that this area is
considered the safest place to indulge in their multifarious
activities, as compared to the strict prohibitive measures
adopted by the authorities of the French Concession in not
allowing such activities and lastly, but not of the least
significance, to the lenient attitude of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council towards them.

The promoters of these organisations which include
many prominent Chinese officials and merchants, were fully
cognisant of the fact that in pursuing their political
activities, they were undoubtedly jeopardising the special
administrative status of the International Settlement and
in this way, an adverse effect on the security of this area
has already been felt. Nevertheless, the Chinese generally
consider that they have every right to utilise this area for
such whatever activities they think fit.

1937年9月28日。第一节。特务科。

中国公共组织 - 政治活动。

随着上海中日敌对行动的爆发，大多数中国公共组织，包括商会及其他具有长期且或多或少受人尊敬地位的团体，开始从事政治运动和宣传。他们的队伍进一步壮大，大量性质不良的组织如雨后春笋般涌现。这些团体的异常政治活动在整个公共租界内引人注目，实际上这些团体的总部或办事处均设于此。这些在某种程度上极不受欢迎的组织存在于租界内，是由于公认的事实：与法租界当局采取严格禁止措施不允许此类活动相比，该地区被视为从事其各种活动的最安全场所；最后但同样重要的是，上海工部局对他们采取了宽容态度。

这些组织的发起者包括许多显赫的中国官员和商人，他们充分意识到，在从事政治活动时，他们无疑危及了公共租界的特殊行政地位，因此，该地区的安全已受到不利影响。然而，中国人普遍认为，他们有权利用该地区进行他们认为合适的任何活动。

An office was established in the Chinese Chamber
of Commerce building, North Soochow Road,
removed to the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's
Association, at the commencement of hostilities,
and again removed to the Doong Nyi Middle School,
63 Avenue Foch. This office was raided by the
French Police. Since then the committee have
kept secret their activities in order to avoid
attention of the foreign authorities. By the
new arrangement, its headquarters is established
in the local Tangpu and 4 separate offices are
secretly maintained, they are :-

1. Kwang Hsia Middle School, 40 Moulmein Road,
where the Propaganda Committee of this
organization is located.

2. Room 504, Pootung Guild, 1454 Avenue Edward
VII, the office of the Secretariat.

3. Doong Nyi Middle School, 63 Avenue Foch,
French Concession - the Secretariat is located.

4. 70 Route Doumer, the residence of Tu Yueh-sung
where the organization committee is located.

All matters for discussion by the committee will
be dealt with by committee members at any place
where they find available. Works performed by
the committee up to the present, as far as
records go to show, consist of the following :-

1. Collection of national salvation contributions
from the public, through local banks and
newspaper offices.

2. Establishment of a War Time Knowledge Class
at 18 Wongkashaw Garden off Carter Road in
conjunction with the local Tangpu. This
class which is attended by about 100
students of local middle schools, commenced
functioning on September 16, and will last
four weeks.

3. Registration and organization of local residents
willing to volunteer for war services. The
registration commenced on August 4, at the
Shanghai Educational Association, 200 Dah Chih
Road, Nantao.

4. Collection of scrap metal from the public, and
allocating of transport and accommodation of same
in case of emergency.

5. On July 30, a resolution was passed that the
people throughout the country be requested to
boycott Japanese goods.

6. On August 18, circular notice issued to local
residents requesting them to contribute money and
articles for comforting the Chinese troops fighting
at the front. On August 19, notices advising
residents to keep indoors and to help in the
relief of refugees, etc. were posted in the
Settlement.

7. On August 22, 12 foreign newspaper reporters were
entertained to dinner in the Sun Sun Restaurant
when the guests were requested not to print
rumours and that they could obtain information
at the Chinese Daily Press Conference in the
Park Hotel.

This committee was formed on the
instructions of the local Kuomintang and
Bureau of Social Affairs, in order to
advise alleyway tenants in the formation
of individual associations for mutual
protection. It was warned by the
Municipal Police to cease activities
on September 8, but on September 16, it
despatched a large quantity of handbills
advising residents to form alleyway
organizations, to the Shanghai Women's
Movement Acceleration Association with
the request that the latter distribute
them among the tenants. The office of
the committee was raided by the Municipal
Police on September 20 when a large
quantity of propaganda matter was seized.

A similar committee was established
in the French Concession at Room 214, Chung
Wei Bank Building, 16 Rue de la Porte du
Nord on August 21, 1937, but it was
later suppressed by the French authorities.

China Times (Noon Issue) :-
Cultural Circles Decide Upon Measures to Commemorate
the September 18 Anniversary

A meeting of representatives of public
bodies was convened yesterday by the propaganda department
of the Cultural Circles' National Extinction Aversion
Association to discuss propaganda programmes in connection
with the 6th anniversary of the September 18 Incident. The
meeting was presided over by Woo Min (吴敏) and two others.
The following resolutions were passed:
(1) That the district be divided into three sections, namely
the Central, the Eastern and the Western Sections and
that the public bodies distribute in their respective
sections on September 18 slogans, pamphlets, pictorial
publications and other printed propaganda matter.
(2) That the public bodies undertake the staging of
theatrical performances, singing of songs and delivering
of speeches or story-telling at the refugee camps and
hospitals for wounded soldiers connected with the
Cultural Circles' National Extinction Aversion Associa-
tion.
(3) That female members of public bodies pay instructional
visits to housewives and their children.

《时报》（午刊）：
文化界决定纪念“九一八”周年措施

文化界救亡协会宣传部昨日召集各公共团体代表开会，讨论与“九一八”事变六周年有关的宣传方案。会议由吴敏等二人主持。通过以下决议：
(1) 将该地区划分为三个部分，即中区、东区和西区，各公共团体于9月18日在各自区域内分发标语、小册子、画报及其他印刷宣传品。
(2) 各公共团体负责在与文化界救亡协会有关的难民营及伤兵医院上演戏剧、演唱歌曲、发表演讲或说书。
(3) 各公共团体的女性成员对家庭主妇及其子女进行指导性访问。
